name: collection
description: The records that match a query, as a live list, table, cards or board: the tasks due this week, the notes tagged garden, the drafts, with the fields a person wants beside each. The same few words pick them here, on the list page, in the assistant's find_records and on the command line.

use.when: a person wants to see what matches, kept current as records change: what is due, what is open, what is tagged.
use.not: one record on its own, which is a record block; or a search for words, which is the search block.
use.with: a heading in label, and a record block or the list page for the full thing.

type.description: The content type, such as task.

where.description: Conditions, all of which must hold. Each is field, operator, value with no spaces: status=draft, done=false, due<today, due<=+7d, title~garden (contains), tags=health (has), notes= for an empty field, due!= for a set one. Dates: 2026-10-01, today, tomorrow, yesterday, now, +7d, -1w. Leave out for every record.

order.description: A field to order by, or -field for the largest or newest first; created_at and updated_at work too. Newest first when left out.

limit.description: How many to show at most.

detail.description: brief is each title as a link with its state; full adds the text.

label.description: The heading over the list, saying what it is: Due this week.

level.description: Heading level of the label so the block fits the page outline.

items.description: Filled in by the server: the matching records. Leave out.

context.description: Filled in by the server only when another item here has the same title: the words that tell this one apart, such as due Fri 25 Sep, read after the title by its link and its box and not shown. Leave out.

at.description: Filled in by the server for a board: the card's id, which a move comes back to.

fields.description: Filled in by the server from show.

href.description: The page of what a ref names, while it exists.

actions.description: Filled in by the server: the one press this record offers, such as Mark as done, as {component, props}. Leave out.

summary.description: Filled in by the server: the conditions in words, shown when nothing matches. Leave out.

all.description: Filled in by the server: the list page with the same query. Leave out.

more.description: Filled in by the server: more matched than the limit shows, so the list says it shows the first of them. Leave out.

problem.description: Filled in by the server when a condition is wrong, saying what the type has instead. Leave out.

as.description: How the matches are shown: list is each title as a link with the chosen fields beside it; table has a column per chosen field; cards are one card each with the fields under the title; board is a column per choice of a pick-list field, such as To do, Doing and Done, with a card for each record in its column.

by.description: For a board, the pick-list field whose choices are the columns, such as status. The first pick-list field of the type when left out.

groups.description: Filled in by the server for a board: its columns, in the order the field lists its choices, then those with none. Leave out.

show.description: Fields to show for each record, by name: due, status, project. A ref shows the title it points at. Leave out for the title and its state alone.

columns.description: Filled in by the server from show: the column headings of a table. Leave out.

titleLabel.description: Filled in by the server: what the title column is called. Leave out.

pressable.description: Filled in by the server: whether the records offer a press, so a table has the column for it. Leave out.

controls.description: Whether the person can narrow and sort the list where it is, with a few choices made from the type's fields: Sort (newest, oldest, A to Z, a date soonest), and a pick-list, a yes-or-no and a date field to show (Not done, Due before today). Their choices only narrow within where, never past it. Left out, they are offered on the block's own page, and on a canvas at full size when more than five match and the limit is over five; false for a short list or a small space, true to offer them anyway.

choices.description: Filled in by the server from controls: the form and what it is showing. Leave out.

action.description: The page the form comes back to, at the list.

keep.description: The page's other address fields, kept as they are.

selects.description: One select's props per choice, shown as a dropdown.

count.description: How many match, in words: 12 tasks.

showing.description: The choices made, in words, when any differ from how it was set up: not done, due soonest first.

reset.description: The same page without this list's choices, when there are any.

keyboard.does: reaches the Sort and Show choices, when offered, and their Apply button, then each record's link, then its checkbox such as Done, then the link to the list page with the same query; What is wrong when the list cannot be shown

wcag.notes: The label is a real heading at the level the outline needs (1.3.1) and names the list for screen readers. Each item is a link with the record's title as its text (2.4.4). An empty result says so in words with the conditions, and a wrong condition says what the type has (3.3.1), rather than rendering nothing. As a table, the title column is a row header and every column has a heading, so each cell is announced with both (1.3.1). As cards, each card's fields are a definition list and its heading sits one level under the list's; as a board, a line over it names each column with how many it holds and leads to it, for a keyboard or switch that cannot move by heading; each column is a section headed one level under the list, with how many it holds in its heading, an empty one saying Nothing in and its name, its cards one level under that, and read column by column so the keyboard follows the reading order; each card has a Move form, the column picked from a list and a Move button named with the card, so a keyboard, a switch, a voice (click Move) and a touch all move it one way with no script, and none drags (2.1.1, 2.5.3, 2.5.7); after a move the page comes back to the card, focused, and says where it went with an Undo; a press anywhere on a card follows its title. In a list, a field shown beside a title has its name in sight, not only for a screen reader. A table that scrolls sideways on a phone is a named region that takes focus, so a keyboard can scroll it (2.1.1). A list cut short by its limit says so, and its link says it has all of them. Each list's heading has an id from its block, so two lists of one type on a page are each named by their own. A person's choices are native selects, each with its label in sight, and an Apply button: changing one changes nothing until Apply, so nothing moves under a keyboard or a screen reader (3.2.2), and it works with no script. After Apply the page comes back at the list, which says how many match and, once, what it is showing, with Reset beside it (3.3.1); a sort is said in words, not by aria-sort, which is for a table's own sortable headers.

machine.identify: Read data-record-type for the type and data-where for the conditions. As a list, each li is one matching record; as a table, each tbody row; as cards, each li holds an article; as a board, each section.sw-collection__column is one choice, its h-element names it, and each li in it holds an article. The first link in each is the record's page.
machine.operate: Change what is shown by updating the block's where, order, limit and detail props. The link with class sw-collection__all opens the list page with the same query, where ?where= and ?order= carry it. A person's own choices are in the page's address as c-<block>-sort and c-<block>-<field>, and narrow data-where without changing it.
